clue.text: Youthful revolutionary song

parts.note: a nursery song for toddlers whose opening line has the wheels going round and round, so it is 'revolutionary' in the turning sense

explanation.surface: A rousing anthem sung by young radicals at the barricades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests political uprising, but here it means turning round, as the wheels in the children's song do.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a famous nursery rhyme sung by small children, about parts of a vehicle that keep turning.

clue.text: Endlessly thrash wild Himalayan creatures

indicators.note: wild suggests letters running out of control into a new order
without its end, so the final letter of the word thrash is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone is told to stop beating ferocious mountain beasts all the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' drops the last H of THRASH, leaving THRAS; 'wild' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahrs are wild goats native to the Himalayan mountains, so they are creatures of that region.

clue.text: At last the politicians accept obligation to dead soldiers

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the following word
to accept is to take in, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: MPs are Members of Parliament
a tie is a binding obligation or commitment

explanation.surface: Finally, the government takes on responsibility for its war dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dead soldiers' is slang for empty bottles, nothing military; 'accept' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead soldiers is slang for drained bottles left after drinking, which are also called empties.

clue.text: Sit on that chair to eat

indicators.note: the words that chair are made to eat, or swallow, the answer, which lies within them

explanation.surface: An instruction to sit on that chair when having a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sit on' seems to go with the chair, but it is the definition, as a bird sits on eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird sits on its eggs to incubate them until the chicks emerge, which is what hatching them means.

clue.text: War and Peace? Not about to provide brief summary

indicators.note: not here asks for the following piece to be left out

parts.note: Tolstoy's novel is both an epic and a huge tome
C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Tolstoy's vast novel is hardly the place to look for a short précis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not about' removes C (circa) from EPIC TOME.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitome is a concise abstract that sums up a longer work in brief.

clue.text: Shift focus to halfwit — extremely easy pickings

indicators.note: shift tells us to move the letters of the words around
the extremes of halfwit are its outer letters

explanation.surface: A tip to change your attention to the dimwit, who is very easily fooled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shift' rearranges FOCUS, TO and H and T, the extreme letters of 'halfwit'.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft touch is a person easily persuaded or exploited, so a source of easy gains.

clue.text: Doing no more than …

definitions.meaning: as in 'what are you ...?', meaning busy with or engaged in
as in '... ten people', meaning at most

explanation.surface: A trailing phrase limiting what someone is doing, leading into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-word phrase means both engaged in an activity and as many as, a limit.

clue.text: Rubbish advice on economy

definitions.meaning: split into two words, the answer tells you to consume less, a tip for saving

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a tip on saving money as nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbish as an adjective means worthless or of no help; split in two the word urges consuming less.

clue.text: Result! Mourinho's front two running riot — United kept looking nervous

indicators.note: the shuffled letters keep, or hold, the next piece inside them
running riot means letters out of control, so they are rearranged
the front two of Mourinho's are its first two letters

parts.note: U is a standard abbreviation for United in team names

explanation.surface: A football match report: the manager's strikers run amok and United are anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: José Mourinho is a football manager. 'Running riot' is the anagram signal and 'kept' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tremulous means trembling or quivering from fear, so it describes someone appearing anxious.

clue.text: … man on road eating dry bread

parts.note: chap is an informal word for a man

indicators.note: eating means taking something inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the A1 is Britain's longest numbered road, written AI
TT, teetotal, means abstaining from alcohol, or dry

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue, a fellow on the road munches stale bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eating' is the container signal. The A1 is the main road from London to Edinburgh; 'dry' as teetotal is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Chapatti is an unleavened flatbread from South Asian cooking.

clue.text: Right to ignore bosses — they're not with us

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: foremen are bosses in charge of workers

explanation.surface: Workers who refuse to obey their managers are no friends of ours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To ignore' removes R from FOREMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Foemen is an archaic word for enemies, those against us rather than with us.

clue.text: Commonly told to look up prophet

indicators.note: said in a common accent that drops the H, so the order 'Eyes 'igher' gives the answer's sound

parts.note: an order to look upwards, like a drill command 'Eyes higher!'

explanation.surface: A seer is told, in ordinary terms, to look up to the heavens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commonly' signals the dropped H of a Cockney accent: 'eyes 'igher' runs into the prophet's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaiah is one of the major Old Testament prophets, with a biblical book named after him.

clue.text: See 1
Old police force's making arrest

parts.note: the Stasi was the secret police of former East Germany
the 's supplies an S

explanation.surface: The former secret police are carrying out a detention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrest' looks like police work, but it is the definition in its sense of stopping.
explanation.definitionFit: Stasis is a state of standstill, and arrest also means a halting of movement or progress.

clue.text: I must — she's around!

indicators.note: around suggests these letters are turned about into another order

explanation.surface: A husband hurries off, realising his wife is nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' rearranges I MUST SHES; the whole clue is also what a husband might say of his wife.
explanation.definitionFit: The missus is a colloquial term for a man's wife, the 'she' he must answer to.

clue.text: What high-fliers do with Alexander in a long-running programme

indicators.note: in places Alexander inside the soaring

parts.note: high-fliers soar up into the sky
Alexander Pope was an 18th-century English poet

explanation.surface: Successful people and someone called Alexander feature in a lengthy TV series.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is the container signal; Alexander is the 18th-century poet, not the conqueror.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap opera is a serial drama on TV or radio that runs for years.

clue.text: Hull extension is only unfinished building — painters use it

parts.note: Rod Hull's puppet Emu was worn on his arm, as an extension of him

indicators.note: building suggests the letters being put together into a new structure
unfinished drops the final letter of only

explanation.surface: An extension to a house in the city of Hull is only half built; decorators use it.
explanation.walkthrough: Rod Hull was a British entertainer whose puppet Emu sat on his arm. 'Building' rearranges IS and ONL.
explanation.definitionFit: Emulsion is a water-based paint widely used by decorators on walls and ceilings.

clue.text: Meet barflies at Saracen's Head — drinks are on us

indicators.note: flies means the letters fly about into a different order
the head of Saracen's is its first letter

explanation.surface: An invitation to meet regulars at a pub called the Saracen's Head, with drinks on the house.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'barflies' must be split, its second half 'flies' being the anagram signal; the Saracen's Head is a common English pub name.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer mats are coasters on which drinks stand, so drinks literally rest on them.

clue.text: Put right clothes on beforehand

indicators.note: beforehand places the piece for on in front

parts.note: re means on or about, as in a letter heading
a dress is an item of clothes; here dress as clothing generally

explanation.surface: Someone is told to dress properly before going out.
explanation.definitionFit: To redress a wrong is to set it right or remedy it.

clue.text: Note allowed in law court

parts.note: so, or soh, is a note of the sol-fa scale
licit means lawful, permitted by law

explanation.surface: A note is permitted as evidence in a court of law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' looks like a law court, but it is a verb: to seek someone's favour.
explanation.definitionFit: To court support or custom is to seek it, as is to solicit it.

clue.text: Straight home on call

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after

parts.note: ho is a call to attract attention, as in 'land ho!'
a nest is a home

explanation.surface: Heading directly home when someone is on call for work.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight in the sense of truthful and upright means trustworthy and frank.

clue.text: Proof of identity sentry looking over

indicators.note: looking over suggests turning over, so the word is reversed in this down entry

parts.note: a gateman guards a gate, like a sentry

explanation.surface: A guard examines someone's ID card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looking over' turns GATEMAN round.
explanation.definitionFit: A badge with a person's name, worn to show who they are.

clue.text: Angry report on Dirty Duck?

parts.note: wild means furious, angry

indicators.note: report suggests a sound heard, so the word for dirty is given by how it is spoken

parts.note: foul means dirty

explanation.surface: A furious review of the Dirty Duck, a pub in Stratford-upon-Avon.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks duck as an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A duck is one example of game birds such as ducks and geese hunted for sport.

clue.text: Ending with half a point — Europe's first

parts.note: demi is a prefix meaning half
S is south, a compass point

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of Europe's

explanation.surface: A sporting finish where Europe win by half a point.
explanation.definitionFit: Demise means death or end, a coming to a close.

clue.text: Passes to Maradona

parts.note: to pass on is to die
to pass is also to go by

explanation.surface: A football commentary: the ball is passed to the Argentine star.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are senses of 'pass': die and go.
explanation.definitionFit: Diego was the first name of the Argentine footballer Maradona.

clue.text: Fit, well and abroad

parts.note: well and so are both conversational fillers, as in 'so, what now?'
und is the German word for and

explanation.surface: Someone is healthy, happy and off on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit, well' looks like a list of synonyms, but only 'Fit' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound means healthy and in good condition, as in sound of mind and body.

clue.text: Untouchable turned on eastern ascetic

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after the next piece
turned means spun round, so the name is read in reverse

parts.note: Eliot Ness led the US agents known as the Untouchables

explanation.surface: An outcast from the caste system rounds on an Eastern holy man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Untouchable' suggests the Indian caste, but it is E. Ness, the Prohibition agent; 'turned' reverses ENESS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Essenes were an ascetic Jewish sect of the Second Temple period.

clue.text: The cuts not initially working — we've heard it lots of times

definitions.text: we've heard it lots of times

indicators.note: working means being worked, kneaded into a new arrangement
initially picks the first letter of not

explanation.surface: A complaint that spending cuts are not working, a familiar refrain.
explanation.definitionFit: A chestnut is a stale joke or story that has been repeated many times.

clue.text: Time off from work demands

indicators.note: off from means taken away from the following word

parts.note: tasks are pieces of work

explanation.surface: Someone asks for leave from their job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off from' removes T from TASKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Asks as a verb means requests or requires, to make demands.

clue.text: In past, cost changed following day (they don't allow for compensation)

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters and F within the word for past

parts.note: ago means in the past

indicators.note: changed means the letters of cost are altered in order

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: Prices that changed the day after, in a dispute over an insurance claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changed' turns the letters of 'cost' into CTSO; 'In' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Insurance policies exclude natural disasters beyond human control, so no payout is made for them.
